dedupe_keys.name: potash mine export supply chain stock policy tested with agent based simulation anylogic case study

description: This vendor case study describes how a global resource company with more than $80 billion in sales, planning a new potash mine that would export 90% of its output, used agent-based simulation to choose a stock management policy for its outbound supply chain by rail to port. The team built an AnyLogic model of the chain and tested push, hybrid and pull policies under different demand, storage and rail capacity scenarios, ranking them on service level, working capital and stock held at the hub and port. It is published by AnyLogic, the simulation software company, and does not name the client. It concerns one mine and export chain. The page is free to read online. Findings: the pull policy was confirmed as best, reaching a 98% service level at lower cost per ton with less working capital, avoiding up to $39 million a year of profit risk and up to $1.2 billion of potential revenue loss, and it proved more resilient to changes in demand and product mix. Caveats: it is marketing material, the figures are the vendor's, and no model or data are shared. For simulation it is an example of testing mine logistics against rail and port capacity limits and demand shocks, a pattern for resilience studies of mineral export chains. It is related to the AnyLogic platform record in this catalogue, the software used.
